name: OASIS (Revi)
question: Does an implantable tibial neuromodulation system powered by an external ankle wearable reduce urgency incontinence episodes by at least 50% in more than half of women with refractory urgency urinary incontinence?

arms.label: Revi implantable tibial neuromodulation system with an external ankle wearable

design.population: 151 implanted women (282 consented) at 23 US and European centers with urgency urinary incontinence (at least nine episodes in a 7-day diary) and an inadequate response to conservative treatment and drugs.
design.description: Prospective, multicenter, single-arm, open-label pivotal device study

verdictNote: Single-arm; the 6-month responder rate exceeded the prespecified 50% performance goal; no comparator group.
takeaway: In 151 women with urgency urinary incontinence in a single-arm pivotal study, the Revi implantable tibial neuromodulation system, powered by an external ankle wearable, produced a 76.4% intention-to-treat responder rate (at least 50% fewer episodes) at 6 months, above the 50% performance goal.

reports.label: Primary 6- and 12-month report
reports.citation: Heesakkers JPFA, Toozs-Hobson P, Sutherland SE, et al. "A prospective study to assess the effectiveness and safety of the BlueWind System in the treatment of patients diagnosed with urgency urinary incontinence." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2024;43(7):1491-1503. doi:10.1002/nau.25477
reports.followUp: 6 and 12 months after activation; primary efficacy at 6 months, primary safety from implantation to 12 months

results.measure: Proportion with at least 50% fewer urgency-related incontinence episodes on a 7-day diary at 6 months after activation; intention-to-treat, imputed for 7 participants with missing 6-month data; performance goal 50%
results.locator: journal p1495, Section 3.2; journal p1500, Discussion
results.note: Null rejected if the lower bound of the two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson interval exceeded 50%. The interval 68.7% to 82.6% is printed in the FDA De Novo summary DEN220073, p19, Table 7, not in the journal text.

results.measure: Same responder definition at 12 months after activation; intention-to-treat, imputed for 12 participants with missing 12-month data
results.note: Not a type I error-controlled endpoint; the FDA De Novo summary (DEN220073, p19) calls the 12-month efficacy analysis post hoc.

results.measure: Responders among participants with a completed 12-month diary
results.locator: journal p1492, Abstract; journal p1501, Discussion
results.note: Paired analysis of the 139 participants with 6- and 12-month diaries: 100/110 (91%) of 6-month responders were responders at 12 months, and 48% of 6-month nonresponders were responders at 12 months.

results.measure: Proportion with at least 10 points improvement in OAB-q health-related quality of life at 6 months; intention-to-treat; performance goal 50%
results.note: 95% CI 76.7% to 88.7%; compared with the 50% performance goal. Tested only after the primary null was rejected (modified Hochberg step-up).

results.endpoint: UUI or large UUI responder rate
results.measure: Proportion with at least 50% fewer urgency-related incontinence episodes or at least 50% fewer large (severe) episodes at 12 months; intention-to-treat; performance goal 50%

Among participants with at least 8 voids/day and at least 9 urgent episodes at baseline (n=113), proportion with at least 50% fewer PPIUS degree 3-4 urgent episodes or fewer than 8 voids/day at 6 months; intention-to-treat
results.note: 95% CI 65.0% to 81.3%. The journal table compares every secondary endpoint with a 50% performance goal; the FDA De Novo summary (DEN220073, p20, Table 8) lists 45% for this endpoint.

results.measure: Mean urgency-related incontinence episodes per day at baseline, 6 months and 12 months, observed data
results.note: Mean change from baseline at 6 months 3.4 (95% CI 2.9 to 3.8); mean percent change 70.3%.

values.exp: 4.8 at baseline; 1.4 at 6 months (n=144); 1.2 at 12 months (n=139)

results.measure: Participants with no leakage on at least 3 consecutive diary days at 12 months
results.note: None were dry at baseline. The 6-month rate is printed as 37.8% (54/144); 54/144 is 37.5%.

results.measure: Symptoms better, much better or very much better at 12 months
results.note: Willingness to continue treatment at 12 months 130/138 (94.2%) on the BSW questionnaire.

results.endpoint: UUI responder rate by prior PTNS
results.measure: Responders in participants with and without prior percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation
results.note: Subgroup comparison without a test; prior PTNS was not an entry requirement and participants were not screened on it.

harms.label: Any adverse event, implantation to 12 months
harms.note: More than 90% of events were not related to the device, treatment or procedure (for example ear infection, cataract, COVID-19).

harms.label: Serious adverse events

values.exp: 15 events in 13/151 participants (8.6%); none related to the procedure or device

harms.note: Relatedness adjudicated by an independent clinical events committee.

harms.label: Device-related adverse events
harms.note: All were pain with stimulation or the implant; five resolved spontaneously, after reprogramming or with antibiotics, although no infection was indicated or confirmed.

harms.label: Procedure-related adverse events
harms.note: Ten (6.6%) were wound-related (7 wound complications, 2 infections, 1 dehiscence), with onset a mean of 19.0 days (range 0 to 67) after implantation and resolution a mean of 28.9 days (range 1 to 65) after onset without sequelae. The other six were numbness after surgery, swollen foot, pain, erythroderma or skin rash, cellulitis and allergic reaction to preoperative medication (1 each). All device- or procedure-related events were mild or moderate.

delivery.label: Enrollment and flow
delivery.value: 282 consented; 151 implanted (87 US, 64 Europe); 9 left before an implant attempt and 11 after implantation; 144 and 140 completed the 6- and 12-month visits

delivery.label: Anesthesia
delivery.value: Local anesthesia in 134/151 (88.7%); the rest had other types such as monitored anesthesia care with sedation; none had regional or general anesthesia

delivery.label: Implant technique
delivery.value: Operating-room placement through an incision of about 5 cm immediately above the ankle; sutured to fascia after intraoperative testing confirmed placement near the posterior tibial neurovascular bundle

delivery.label: Investigator training and sites
delivery.value: 23 sites in the US and Europe; investigators had SNM and PTNS experience and completed didactic sessions with cadaveric training or proctoring for first implantations

delivery.label: Activation and stimulation settings
delivery.value: Activation within 4 (plus or minus 2) weeks of implantation; default 14 Hz and 210 microseconds; range 2-30 Hz, 190-790 microseconds, 0.2-10 mA; about 30-60 minutes and no more than 120 minutes of use daily

delivery.label: Compliance
delivery.value: At least 1 treatment per day in more than 90% of participants at every follow-up visit; 91.6% compliance across 12 months
delivery.locator: journal p1496, Section 3.4; journal p1501, Discussion

delivery.label: Intention-to-treat imputation
delivery.value: Data imputed for 7 participants missing 6-month data and 12 missing 12-month data; one participant explanted before the 9-month visit counted as a treatment failure

reports.dateLocator: Europe PMC and PubMed electronic publication date
reports.citation: Heesakkers JPFA, Toozs-Hobson P, Sutherland SE, et al. "Two-Year Efficacy and Safety Outcomes of the Pivotal OASIS Study Using the Revi System for Treatment of Urgency Urinary Incontinence." *J Urol.* 2025;213(3):323-332. doi:10.1097/JU.0000000000004328
reports.followUp: 24 months after activation; 97 of 151 implanted participants had 24-month diary data
reports.followUpLocator: Results, Study Population and Follow-Up and Durable Reduction sections

results.measure: Completers analysis: at least 50% fewer urgency-related incontinence episodes at 24 months on a 3-day diary
results.note: Response rates among participants with data were 78% at 6 months, 82% at 12 months and 79% at 24 months. Descriptive statistics only; no confidence interval or p value.

results.measure: Completers analysis at 24 months

results.endpoint: UUI responder rate, last observation carried forward
results.measure: All implanted participants, last available visit carried forward; explanted participants counted as failures
results.note: The denominator is not printed in the article text; the table is in Supplementary Table ST6.

results.measure: Participants with at least 50% fewer UUI episodes at one or more follow-up visits, among 149 with at least one post-activation visit
Completers at 24 months
Mean urgency-related leaks per day, baseline to 24 months
results.note: Large urgency-related leaks fell from 0.9 to 0.1 per day; voids per day from 10.0 to 8.3.

results.measure: At least 50% fewer moderate-to-severe urgency episodes (PPIUS degree 3-4) or normalized voids at 24 months
Satisfied with therapy on the BSW questionnaire at 24 months
results.locator: Results, Reported Improvements in QOL section
results.note: Patient Global Impression of Improvement better to very much better 94/97 (96.9%); willingness to continue 94/94 (100%); all OAB-q domains improved by more than 10 points (n=94).

harms.label: Device- or procedure-related serious adverse events through 24 months
harms.note: In months 12 to 24, 117 adverse events were reported and 116 were unrelated to the device or procedure; relatedness was adjudicated by site investigators after 12 months.

harms.label: Late surgical-site event
harms.note: A delayed superficial skin infection from an exuded nonabsorbable braided suture, managed without explantation.

harms.label: Explantation through 24 months
harms.note: Pacemaker need (contraindicated at the time); musculoskeletal complications after an unrelated fall; one at a nonresponder's request in year 2. None was due to a device- or procedure-related adverse event. No device migrations or revision procedures.

delivery.label: Participant flow
delivery.value: 140 completed 12 months; 121 consented to long-term follow-up and 2 failed rescreening; 14 stopped before 24 months (8/14 responders); 97 completed the 24-month assessment
delivery.locator: Results, Study Population and Follow-Up section and Figure 2

delivery.label: Stimulation regimen
delivery.value: At least two 30-minute sessions daily (up to 2 hours) in year 1, then at the physician's and patient's discretion with at least two 30-minute sessions per week; on average at least 1 session on 8 of every 10 days in year 2
delivery.locator: Methods, Stimulation Therapy Application; Results, Study Population and Follow-Up section

reports.label: Quality-of-life analysis through 24 months
reports.citation: Sutherland SE, Heesakkers JPFA, Ferrante KL, Dmochowski RR. "Impact of Revi Implantable Tibial Neuromodulation on Quality of Life in Patients with Urgency Urinary Incontinence." *Int Urogynecol J.* 2026;37(8):2451-2461. doi:10.1007/s00192-026-06538-2
reports.followUp: Through 24 months after activation; completers analysis

results.measure: Proportion with at least a 10-point improvement in total transformed HRQL score, completers, at 6, 12 and 24 months
results.locator: Results, Overactive Bladder and Health-Related Quality of Life section
results.note: Mean total HRQL score rose from 46.6 (n=149) to 83.3 (n=96) at 24 months.

values.exp: 83.1% of 142 at 6 months; 85.4% of 137 at 12 months; 87.2% of 94 at 24 months

results.endpoint: Benefit, satisfaction and willingness to continue
results.measure: BSW questionnaire at 24 months
results.locator: Results, Benefit, Satisfaction, and Willingness to Continue section; Table 3

results.endpoint: BSW in participants below the responder threshold
results.measure: Among 20 participants (20.6% of 97) with less than a 50% reduction in UUI episodes at 24 months; 18 completed the BSW
results.locator: Results, Quality-of-Life Outcomes in Participants Without 50% Reduction section
results.note: In these 20 participants the mean reduction in UUI episodes was 20.3%.

harms.label: Adverse events through 24 months

values.exp: 414 events, of which 7 device-related and 18 procedure-related

harms.note: All mild to moderate; no device- or procedure-related serious adverse events; 3/151 explants (2%) unrelated to device- or procedure-related adverse events; no migrations or revisions.

results.measure: Completers analysis: at least 50% fewer urgency-related incontinence episodes at 36 months on a 3-day diary
results.note: Response rates were 78%, 82%, 79% and 79% at 6, 12, 24 and 36 months among participants with data. Descriptive statistics; the 6-month rate was 112/144 (78%).

Completers on a 3-day diary at 36 months
Mean urgency-related leaks per day, baseline to 36 months
results.note: Voids per day fell from 10.0 to 8.1 and nocturia from 1.28 to 0.88 per day.

results.measure: At least 50% fewer moderate-to-severe urgency episodes (PPIUS degree 3-4) or normalized voids at 36 months
Satisfied with therapy on the BSW questionnaire at 36 months
results.locator: Results, Reported Improvements in Quality of Life section
results.note: Patient Global Impression of Improvement much better or very much better 74/90 (82%); willing to continue 85/87 (98%).

harms.label: Device- or procedure-related serious adverse events through 36 months
harms.note: 543 adverse events in total through 36 months.

harms.label: Device-related adverse events through 36 months
harms.note: Primarily pain, discomfort, burning or a stimulation issue; none serious. Seven events in 6 participants (4.0%) occurred between 24 and 36 months.

harms.label: Surgical wound-related events through 36 months
harms.note: None serious. One procedure-related infection between 12 and 24 months; one infection and one granuloma in 2 participants (1.3%) between 24 and 36 months.

harms.label: Explantation through 36 months
harms.note: Two in the first 12 months; two for painful stimulation (753 and 1,230 days after implantation); one at 1,233 days for foot fusion surgery. No device migrations or revision procedures.

delivery.label: Participant flow
delivery.value: 140 completed 12 months; 121 consented to the extension and 2 failed rescreening (119); 27 stopped early; 90 provided 36-month diary data
delivery.locator: Abstract; Results, Study Population and Follow-Up section and Figure 2

delivery.label: Daily use at 36 months
delivery.value: At least 1 session daily in 69/90 (77%); fewer than 1 daily by patient choice in 21/90 (23%)

delivery.label: Implant technique
delivery.value: Operating-room placement, subfascial at the medial ankle through an incision of about 5 cm, abutting the posterior tibial neurovascular bundle; intraoperative testing raised stimulation until paresthesia in the heel, sole or toe before the lead was secured to the crural fascia

relations.note: Single-arm pivotal study of a newer implanted neuromodulator for urgency incontinence, sacral rather than tibial, judged against a 50% responder goal.
